newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah rockets Israeli targets in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah rockets Israeli targets in south Lebanon.

text.p: Pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas fired Katyusha rockets into Israeli and allied militia posts in south Lebanon on Tuesday, a day after Israeli shelling killed two Lebanese civilians, Hizbollah said.

Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia sources said a number of Katyushas fell near the Israeli outpost of Blat and the SLA outposts of Dimeshkieeh and Risha inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, causing no damage or casualty.
"The Katyusha rocketing was in response for the continued violation of April 1996 understanding which bans firing on civilians," a Hizbollah spokesman told Reuters.

The April 1996 ceasefire understanding which ended 17 days of an Israeli onslaught on Lebanon in which about 200 people -- mainly civilians -- were killed, bars Israel and Hizbollah from hitting civilian targets.

Israeli shelling on Monday night killed two civilians in the village of Berti, east of the southern port city of Sidon. The shelling occurred after two SLA militiamen were wounded in a Hizbollah rocket attack on their outpost.
Israeli warplanes also raided suspected Hizbollah positions in the south.
The 3,000-strong SLA militia helps some 1,000 Israeli troops hold a 15-km (nine miles)-deep occupation zone in south Lebanon.
Hizbollah (Party of God) frequently attacks Israeli and SLA posts and patrols in a bid to drive the Israelis from the occupation zone.
